section_header: EMISSION CONTROL SYSTEMS — Exhaust Gas Recirculation (EGR) System
title: INSPECTION OF EGR VALVE

content.text: 1. CHECK AND CLEAN FILTER IN EGR VACUUM MODULATOR

items: (a) Check the filter for contamination or damage.
(b) Using compressed air, clean the filter.

content.description: EGR vacuum modulator assembly showing filter location and components in exploded view

content.text: Disconnect the vacuum hose from the EGR valve and, using a three way union, connect a vacuum gauge to it.

content.description: Vacuum gauge connected to EGR system via three-way union with multiple hoses

content.text: Start the engine and check that the engine starts and runs at idle.

items: (a) The coolant temperature should be below 57°C (135°F).
(b) Check that the vacuum gauge indicates zero at 2,500 rpm.

content.description: Two gauge displays showing tachometer at 2,500 rpm and vacuum gauge reading for cold engine test

content.text: 5. CHECK VSV AND EGR VACUUM MODULATOR WITH WARM ENGINE

items: (b) Check that the vacuum gauge indicates about 70 mm Hg (2.76 in.Hg, 9.3 kPa) at 2,500 rpm.
(c) Check that the vacuum gauge indicates zero at idle.

content.description: Two gauge displays showing tachometer at 2,500 rpm and vacuum gauge reading showing low vacuum for hot engine test

items: (d) Disconnect the vacuum hose from R port of the EGR vacuum modulator and connect R port directly to the intake manifold with another hose.
(e) Check that the vacuum gauge indicates high vacuum at 2,500 rpm.

content.text: NOTE: As a large amount of EGR gas enters, the engine will misfire.

items: (f) Disconnect the vacuum gauge and reconnect the vacuum hoses to the proper locations.

content.description: Vacuum gauge being connected to EGR system showing direct connection setup
